title: Habitat connectivity shapes biodiversity outcomes in Indonesia's community‐managed forests
content:
Our findings suggest that community-managed forests established within predominantly forested areas can make a meaningful contribution to area-based conservation, including recognition as Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs). In community-managed forests established in more modified production landscapes, targeted restoration and actions that enhance habitat connectivity are likely required to sustain populations of priority species. Ensuring that social forestry policies explicitly incorporate biodiversity incentives and connectivity-led management can help align community development objectives with global conservation goals.

Abstract

Social forestry is increasingly promoted as a means to achieve equitable resource governance while contributing to biodiversity conservation. Yet, empirical evidence on how effectively community-managed forests support biodiversity remains limited, particularly in tropical regions. We assessed mammal communities in two contrasting social forestry contexts in Sumatra, Indonesia: (1) a forest-dominated landscape where management emphasised forest retention, and (2) an agroforestry-mosaic characterised by mixed production systems and forest remnants. Using camera-trap data and hierarchical multi-species occupancy models, we compared species richness, community occupancy and the occurrence of forest specialists and globally threatened species between social forestry areas and adjacent watershed protection forests. We also assessed the influence of five environmental (structural connectivity, biomass, forest cover and terrain ruggedness) and anthropogenic (quantified using remoteness) factors in shaping species' occurrence patterns across these multiple-use landscapes. Overall species richness and community occupancy in community-managed forests were comparable to protection forests in both landscapes. However, community composition diverged depending on the landscape context. In the forest-dominated landscape, occupancy of forest specialists and threatened taxa was maintained, while generalist species showed higher occupancy in social forestry areas. Conversely, in the agroforestry-mosaic, forest specialists and threatened taxa had reduced occupancy within social forestry areas, largely driven by lower forest quality and diminished structural connectivity in some areas. Forest structural connectivity emerged as the strongest environmental driver of mammal occurrence. High connectivity buffered biodiversity losses in the forest-dominated community forests, whereas reduced connectivity in the agroforestry-mosaic landscape amplified declines among species with greater forest dependencies. Remoteness further influenced occurrence patterns, particularly favouring forest specialists in the forest-dominated landscape. Synthesis and applications. Our findings suggest that community-managed forests established within predominantly forested areas can make a meaningful contribution to area-based conservation, including recognition as Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs). In community-managed forests established in more modified production landscapes, targeted restoration and actions that enhance habitat connectivity are likely required to sustain populations of priority species. Ensuring that social forestry policies explicitly incorporate biodiversity incentives and connectivity-led management can help align community development objectives with global conservation goals.

Abstrak

Perhutanan sosial semakin dipromosikan sebagai sarana untuk mencapai tata kelola sumber daya yang adil serta berkontribusi pada konservasi keanekaragaman hayati. Namun, bukti empiris tentang seberapa efektif hutan yang dikelola masyarakat mendukung keanekaragaman hayati masih terbatas, terutama di wilayah tropis. Kami menilai komunitas mamalia dalam dua konteks perhutanan sosial yang kontras di Sumatra, Indonesia: (1) lanskap yang didominasi hutan di mana pengelolaan berfokus pada retensi hutan, dan (2) mosaik agroforestri dengan karakter sistem produksi campuran dan sisa-sisa hutan. Menggunakan data perangkap kamera dan model okupansi multi-spesies hierarkis, kami membandingkan kekayaan spesies, okupansi komunitas satwa, dan kehadiran satwa spesialis hutan serta spesies yang terancam secara global antara kawasan perhutanan sosial dan kawasan hutan lindung daerah aliran air yang berdekatan. Kami juga menilai pengaruh lima faktor lingkungan (konektivitas struktural, biomassa, tutupan hutan, dan indeks kekasaran medan) dan antropogenik (dikuantifikasi menggunakan keterpencilan) dalam membentuk pola keberadaan spesies di seluruh lanskap multi-fungsi ini. Kekayaan spesies secara keseluruhan dan okupansi komunitas satwa di hutan yang dikelola masyarakat sebanding dengan hutan lindung di kedua lanskap. Namun, komposisi komunitas satwa bervariasi tergantung pada konteks lanskap. Di lanskap yang didominasi hutan, okupansi satwa spesialis hutan dan taksa terancam tetap terjaga, sementara spesies generalis menunjukkan okupansi yang lebih tinggi di area perhutanan sosial. Sebaliknya, di mosaik agroforestri, spesialis hutan dan taksa terancam mengalami penurunan okupansi di dalam kawasan perhutanan sosial, sebagian besar didorong oleh kualitas hutan yang lebih rendah dan konektivitas struktural yang berkurang di beberapa lokasi. Konektivitas lanskap muncul sebagai faktor pendorong lingkungan terkuat bagi keberadaan mamalia. Konektivitas tinggi menahan kehilangan keanekaragaman hayati di perhutanan masyarakat yang didominasi tegakan hutan, sementara konektivitas yang berkurang di lanskap mosaik agroforestri mendorong penurunan populasi spesies yang sangat bergantung dengan hutan. Keterpencilan lebih lanjut mempengaruhi pola keberadaan satwa, khususnya mendukung satwa spesialis hutan di lanskap yang didominasi hutan. Implikasi dan aplikasi praktis. Temuan kami menunjukkan bahwa hutan yang dikelola masyarakat dalam kawasan yang didominasi tegakan hutan dapat memberikan kontribusi bermakna untuk konservasi berbasis wilayah, termasuk pengakuan sebagai Upaya Konservasi Berbasis Kawasan yang efektif lainnya (OECMs). Di hutan yang dikelola masyarakat dalam lanskap produksi yang lebih termodifikasi, restorasi yang sesuai sasaran dan tindakan yang meningkatkan konektivitas habitat cukup diperlukan untuk mempertahankan populasi spesies prioritas. Memastikan bahwa kebijakan perhutanan sosial secara eksplisit menggabungkan insentif keanekaragaman hayati dan pengelolaan yang berbasis konektivitas dapat membantu menyelaraskan tujuan pembangunan masyarakat dengan tujuan konservasi global.
